outline.h2: What is a UX strategy roadmap, and how is it different from a product roadmap?
outline.answerHint: A UX strategy roadmap is a time-bound plan that turns a UX strategy into prioritized themes, each a user problem with evidence, a RICE score, one success metric, an owner and a horizon. A product roadmap lists features and release dates; a UX strategy roadmap lists the user problems the product team will solve and how it will know they are solved.
points: Intro before this H2 (before/after row intro, see variety): open with one bad roadmap row ('Q2: redesign the settings page') and, two sentences later, the same row rewritten as a theme (user, problem, evidence, metric, owner). Keyword in the first sentence (carrier above). Then 2 sentences on what the post gives: the inputs, the scoring, the metrics, a one-page example and the review rhythm.
UP link to the hub within the first 300 words: anchor 'UX consulting services' (e.g. 'the prioritized roadmap is the main output of our UX consulting services').
Name the parent: a UX strategy roadmap sits under a UX strategy (the goal, users and success measures); expand 'user experience (UX)' and use 'user experience roadmap' once here.

Answer 'what is UX strategy' in one or two sentences as the layer above the roadmap (secondary carrier), and define the UX strategy document as the half page that holds it. Do not build a definition section on UX strategy itself (future TOFU post).

Table, introduced by one sentence: UX strategy roadmap vs product roadmap vs fix roadmap vs product backlog. Columns: what each row is, time span, who owns it, what it is measured by. The fix roadmap row: a UX audit hands over a prioritized fix roadmap of interface issues (the one cross-hub link: /services/ux-audit-services/ with anchor 'fix roadmap from a UX audit'). Visual 1 is this table (see visuals); text version under it. Cite NN/g's definition (Sarah Gibbons, 2020) in our own words.

outline.h2: What evidence does a UX strategy roadmap need before anyone draws it?
outline.answerHint: A UX strategy roadmap needs five inputs before the product team writes a single theme: 6–10 stakeholder interviews, GA4 funnel data, past research and usability testing findings, support and sales feedback, and a UX maturity score. Without them, the prioritized themes are opinions.
points: Numbered list (ol) of the 5 inputs, each with what it tells the roadmap. Stakeholder interviews: 6–10 leads from product, engineering, sales and support (hub figure). GA4: funnel step drop-offs and the activation rate baseline. Research: past interviews and usability testing clips. Support tags and sales loss reasons. UX maturity: score the company on the Nielsen Norman Group 6-stage model (Absent, Limited, Emergent, Structured, Integrated, User-driven; fact-checker to confirm stage names on nngroup.com).
Evidence level attribute: tag every input research, analytics or opinion; this tag later becomes the confidence score in RICE.
Maturity point (SERP gap): a company at an early stage gets research and process themes before redesign themes.
Visual 2: evidence ledger card (see visuals).

Lead moment 1: interviewing 6–10 leaders who disagree is where an outside facilitator earns its fee; one natural sentence ('we run these interviews in the first 2–3 days of an engagement'), no invented claims.

outline.h2: How do you turn user problems into roadmap themes?
outline.answerHint: Group the evidence into 5–8 themes, each written as a user problem with a beneficiary and a need, never as a feature. 'Admins cannot invite a team without support' is a theme; 'redesign settings' is not.
points: First sentence must name 'UX roadmap' or 'UX strategy roadmap' + 'prioritized themes' (essential concepts).
Jobs to be Done phrasing for the problem statement (one line: 'When…, I want to…, so I can…'), with one example. Hub entity; explain it in one sentence.
Visual 3: feature-to-theme rewrite (before/after, 4 rows). Rows are our own illustrative examples (settings, onboarding, reporting export, mobile parity); text version under the image.
Design debt can be a theme only when tied to a user problem (e.g. inconsistent tables slow task success); one sentence.
Keep themes to a number leadership can hold: 5–8 is our working rule (label as our practice, not a statistic).

outline.h2: How do you score the themes on a UX strategy roadmap with RICE?
outline.answerHint: Score each of the prioritized themes with RICE: reach (users affected per quarter) x impact (0.25 to 3) x confidence (50%, 80% or 100%, set by the evidence level) / effort (person-weeks). The highest RICE score goes first unless a dependency blocks it.
points: Cite Intercom's RICE article (Sean McBride) for the formula and scales: impact 3 massive, 2 high, 1 medium, 0.5 low, 0.25 minimal; confidence 100% high, 80% medium, 50% low; effort in person-months in the original. We use person-weeks for UX themes: say so as our adaptation. Fact-checker: confirm the scales on the live Intercom page.
Tie confidence to the evidence level from H2 2: usability testing or analytics = 100%, mixed = 80%, stakeholder opinion only = 50%. This is the post's first-hand rule; label it as our practice.

Visual 4: RICE scoring card with 5 illustrative themes (invented inputs, captioned 'illustrative'); the text version holds the table. Show one theme where high confidence beats a bigger but unproven idea.
One sentence on alternatives: MoSCoW and value vs effort are faster but give no shared number; do not build a comparison section of methods (NN/g has a 5-methods article; do not mirror it).

Lead moment 2: a scored list with effort agreed by engineering is the step most in-house roadmaps skip; the hub's 'maturity scoring and strategy' step does this in 2–4 days (deep link to /services/ux-consulting-services/#how-does-the-ux-consulting-process-work).

outline.h2: Which success metric proves each theme worked?
outline.answerHint: Give each theme on the UX roadmap one success metric from the Google HEART framework, chosen through Goals-Signals-Metrics: happiness, engagement, adoption, retention or task success. The product team writes the baseline from GA4 and a target before work starts.
points: First sentence must carry 'UX strategy roadmap' or 'UX roadmap' + 'prioritized themes' or 'product team'.

Cite Rodden, Hutchinson and Fu (Google, CHI 2010) for HEART and Goals-Signals-Metrics. Explain each of the 5 categories in one clause with a UX theme example (task success: share of admins who finish an invite without help).
Visual 5: HEART goals-signals-metrics grid for 3 illustrative themes (see visuals).
Link the roadmap metric to company objectives and key results (OKRs) in one or two sentences: the theme metric is the key result a product team reports.
Activation rate as the example metric for an onboarding theme (hub benefit wording: 'the share of new users who reach the first key action'). No uplift figure.

outline.h2: How do you place themes on now, next and later horizons?
outline.answerHint: A UX roadmap puts a theme in 'now' only when it has high confidence, a named owner and product team capacity this quarter; 'next' holds prioritized themes waiting on capacity or a dependency; 'later' holds low-confidence themes whose first task is research.
points: Three rules as a ul (one per horizon), with the roadmap horizon attribute in quarters. Credit NN/g for the now/next/future idea in one clause; our wording is now, next and later.
Key move: a low-confidence theme does not wait idle; its 'next' item is a usability testing round or interview study that raises confidence.
No image here (image budget; the one-page example in H2 8 shows the horizons).
Dates: use quarters, not days, beyond 'now' (time horizons entity).

outline.h2: Who owns the roadmap, and what does the roadmap workshop decide?
outline.answerHint: One roadmap owner (usually the head of product or design) keeps the UX strategy roadmap, and each of the prioritized themes has one named theme owner. The roadmap workshop, about 2 hours with leadership and the product team, agrees owners, horizons and the metric for each theme.
points: Decision rights as a short ul: who can add a theme, who can move a theme between horizons, who can kill one (our practice; label it).

Workshop agenda as an ol in 4–5 blocks (evidence recap, scores, objections, owners and dates, next review date). Hub fact: the roadmap is presented in a 2-hour workshop where owners and dates are agreed. Tools: a FigJam board (or a slide), one sentence, no tool comparison.

DOWN link to the Mass Media Co. case study: 'we ran a discovery workshop with MMC stakeholders and users… covered product definition, strategy, information architecture and user flows'. Use only that sentence's facts. Do not attribute the 30% order processing efficiency to the workshop or to a roadmap; Mass Media Co. was a product revamp, not a UX consulting engagement (its services list does not include ux-consulting-services).
Disambiguate 'workshop' as a roadmap workshop with stakeholders, not a UX strategy training course.

outline.h2: UX strategy roadmap example: one page for a B2B SaaS onboarding problem
outline.answerHint: This UX strategy roadmap example fits on one page: a three-line strategy statement on top, then five prioritized themes across now, next and later, each with its RICE score, HEART metric and owner. The company and numbers are illustrative.
points: Label the whole example illustrative (invented company, invented numbers). Reuse the 5 themes from the RICE card so the numbers match across visuals.
Top block = the UX strategy document (secondary carrier): goal, primary users, the user problem the year is about, success measures.
Visual 6: one-page roadmap board (see visuals). The text version under it is the full example in table form (theme | horizon | RICE score | metric and target | owner).
Point out 2 things the reader can copy: research themes sit in 'next' to raise confidence, and every 'now' theme has a baseline.
This is the only 'UX strategy roadmap + noun' stack counted in the H2s.

outline.h2: How often should you review the UX strategy roadmap, and when should you get help?
outline.answerHint: Review the UX strategy roadmap with the product team every quarter and check progress monthly: update scores with new evidence, move themes between horizons and retire themes whose metric hit target. Bring in outside help when leaders disagree on the prioritized themes or no one has time to collect the evidence.
points: Review cadence attribute: a monthly 30-minute check (status, blocked themes) and a quarterly review (re-score, re-horizon, maturity check). Hub fact: quarterly roadmap reviews develop UX maturity one stage at a time. The 30-minute length is our practice; label it.

Mistakes as reasoned bullets (mistake + why): features instead of problems; no baseline; every theme 'now'; scores set by the loudest stakeholder; no owner; roadmap never revisited. Keep to 5–6 bullets.

When to get help: link the hub section 'When should a leadership team hire UX consulting services?' (/services/ux-consulting-services/#when-should-a-leadership-team-hire-ux-consulting-services) instead of listing its 5 situations.

Main lead moment and offer (see leadAngle). Second UP link with the price: engagement price and engagement duration stated once, in hub wording, with the deep link /services/ux-consulting-services/#how-much-does-ux-consulting-cost. Close with /contact/ ('send us your current roadmap or backlog').

faqs.q: What should a UX roadmap include?
faqs.hint: Short list in one answer: strategy statement, themes as user problems, evidence level, RICE score, one success metric with baseline and target, theme owner, roadmap horizon and the next review date. Same answer as H2 1 and H2 8 (one intent, one answer).

faqs.q: Who should create the UX roadmap?
faqs.hint: The head of product or design owns it; designers, product managers, engineering and research contribute evidence and effort estimates; leadership agrees it in the roadmap workshop. 2–3 sentences.

faqs.q: How long does it take to build a UX strategy roadmap?
faqs.hint: Hub fact: our engagement takes 2–3 weeks (10–15 working days) from the first stakeholder interview to the roadmap workshop. Do not repeat Entropik's 'less than a day'. One sentence that a team with evidence already gathered can draft one faster; no invented number.

faqs.q: Is a UX roadmap the same as a UX research roadmap?
faqs.hint: No. A UX research roadmap plans studies only; a UX strategy roadmap holds research themes and design themes, and research items exist to raise confidence in a theme. 2 sentences. Do not link the research hub here (the one cross-hub link goes to the audit hub).

faqs.q: Can a UX strategy roadmap work with OKRs?
faqs.hint: Yes. Each theme's success metric becomes a key result under a company objective; the roadmap shows which themes serve which objective. 2 sentences.

4 illustrative rows: left 'feature row' in grey (e.g. 'Redesign settings', 'New onboarding', 'Export button', 'Mobile parity'), right 'theme' (user + problem + evidence). Arrow between columns. Text version under the image.

5 themes x columns reach | impact | confidence | effort (person-weeks) | RICE score, sorted by score; confidence cells coloured by evidence level. Caption says illustrative. Text version = the same table.
3 illustrative themes x columns HEART category | goal | signal | metric | baseline -> target. Text version under the image.

Strategy statement band on top (goal, users, problem, success measures), then three swimlanes now / next / later with the 5 theme cards from the RICE card (score, metric, owner as a role, no real names). Landscape. Caption says illustrative. Text version = the example table.

leadAngle: Three moments. (1) End of the evidence section: 6–10 leaders who disagree are hard to interview from inside; we run these interviews in the first 2–3 days of an engagement (hub step). (2) End of the RICE section: a scored list with engineering-agreed effort is what in-house roadmaps usually skip; our maturity scoring and strategy step does it in 2–4 days (deep link to the process). (3) Main offer in the review section: send us your current roadmap or backlog, and in a free consultation we point out which rows are features rather than problems and what evidence is missing; the full engagement delivers the prioritized UX strategy roadmap, HEART metrics and the 2-hour roadmap workshop in 2–3 weeks for $5,000–$15,000 (hub cost section link), with quarterly roadmap reviews as ongoing advisory if wanted. MOFU template CTA = case study + consultation: Mass Media Co. is the case to feature. Do not promise a written review of their roadmap before the call (not a published offer).

variety.introStyle: before/after roadmap row (one feature-style row, then the same row rewritten as a scored theme). Last 9 intros used: buyer scenario, myth, data point with source, question, definition, mini case, contrarian take, itemized receipt, 60-second phone test. Not a repeat.
h2Frames: what is X and how is it different
how often to review + when to get help
variety.sectionOrder: row-rewrite intro -> definition + four-roadmap table -> evidence ledger -> problem-to-theme rewrite -> RICE scoring -> HEART metrics -> horizon rules -> ownership + workshop agenda (Mass Media Co.) -> one-page example -> review cadence, mistakes, help + price link -> FAQs
variety.ctaAngle: send us your current roadmap or backlog -> free consultation on which rows are features, not problems; Mass Media Co. workshop as the case study
variety.listStyle: numbered evidence inputs + scored table + horizon rules + workshop agenda ol + mistake bullets (mistake + why)
variety.differsFrom: Last 3 site-wide: ecommerce-ux-audit (Checklist / 60-second phone test), usability-testing-cost-per-participant (Guide / itemized receipt), mobile-app-design-agency-vs-freelancer (Comparison / contrarian take). Differs on intro, H2 frames, section order, visuals, CTA angle and list style (6 of 7; type Guide matches the post 2 back). Silo has no posts. Nearest structural relatives: (a) design-system-roi (formula + worked example + business case): do NOT reuse its formula-anatomy visual, input worksheet, break-even chart or 'one-page business case' wording; our one-pager is a roadmap board, not a business case. (b) ecommerce-ux-audit (severity x reach / effort priority 2x2): do NOT use a 2x2 or its quadrant labels; RICE is a ranked table. (c) web-app-design-rfp ('weak-to-priceable rewrites' visual): our before/after is roadmap rows; keep the visual style different (two columns with an arrow, not strike-through edits).

notes: Exact keyword 'ux strategy roadmap' in title/H1, slug, first sentence, description (prescribed, 150 chars), first meta keyword. No keyword or secondary contains 'vs'. H2 1 says 'different from a product roadmap' as a question, with no 'vs' string.

Cannibalisation, hub (content/services/ux-consulting-services.json, anchor 'UX consulting services', metaTitle 'UX Consulting Services | Senior UX Strategy & Roadmaps'): it owns what UX consulting is, the 6 deliverables, the 4-step process, benefits, 'UX consulting vs UX audit', cost, 'when to hire' and FAQs (what a UX consultant does, ongoing, design work, duration). Its metaTitle says 'Roadmaps' and its ngrams include 'ux strategy roadmap', but the hub is a service page and the query SERP is how-to (NN/g, Maze, Entropik, ProCreator), so the post serves the informational intent the hub cannot. Mitigation: the post never defines UX consulting, never prices it on its own terms (deep link), never uses 'UX consultant' or 'UX consulting' in an H2, and links up twice. Hub banking: see backlinkSuggestions #1.

Other pages: grep of content/ for 'ux strategy', 'ux roadmap', 'strategy roadmap' found the term only on the hub and in passing links on 2 location pages, about.md, home.ts, the design-system and ux-research hubs. 'fix roadmap' belongs to the ux-audit hub (metaTitle 'Heuristic Review & Fix Roadmap'): use it only in the comparison row with the cross-hub link, never as a heading. No blog post or brief targets strategy or roadmaps.

Future silo posts (all with Ahrefs volume, 2026-10-17): TOFU 'ux strategy' (800/0) + 'ux design strategy' (700/0) + 'what is ux strategy' (200/5) + 'ux strategy definition' (150/0) + 'why ux design strategy is important' (150/3) as ONE definition post; its SERP is definitions (careerfoundry, uxdesigninstitute, uxcel, trymata, coursera, oreilly). This brief answers 'what is UX strategy' in only 1–2 sentences so that post stays open. BOFU still open: the commercial terms in the pull ('ux strategy consulting/agency/services', 'ux consulting firms/company', 'top ux strategy agency') are the hub head term or listicles; the next BOFU should test a non-head buyer angle (e.g. 'ux consultant vs agency' or 'ux consultant hourly rate'), both NEED VOLUME. Do not give the next post a RICE or HEART section (owned here).

Case studies: grep of content/case-studies for strategy/roadmap/stakeholder/workshop: Mass Media Co. ('discovery workshop with MMC stakeholders and users… product definition, strategy, information architecture and user flows') is the only workshop description; TradeZella ('discovery sessions with the stakeholders to understand their long-term vision') is the only other. Neither lists ux-consulting-services in its services, so present them as examples of stakeholder workshops in a product revamp, never as UX consulting engagements, and do not attribute their results (MMC +30% order processing efficiency; any TradeZella figure) to a roadmap or workshop.

Honesty, do not use: ProCreator's 'nearly 6 in 10 SaaS businesses fail to reach profitability' (secondhand via Userpilot), its 25%/30%/20%/15% metric targets and 'companies that iterate often see higher engagement'; Entropik's 'less than a day' and 'more than a month' durations; the home.ts telehealth '130+ facilities' frontstage/backstage anecdote (no case study). Every worked example uses invented inputs and says 'illustrative'. No uplift percentage for any theme.

Originality: beats page procreator.design (what is -> 6 steps: vision, journey, themes, prioritize, develop, iterate -> UX vs product roadmap -> when (5 stages) -> FAQ: how to create, tools, how often). Do not use its 6-step H2/H3 order, its 'when should you build' lifecycle list, its quarterly Q1–Q4 table layout, its 0–3/3–6/6+ month phases or its 3 FAQs in the same wording. Maze/Entropik: no 'product / field / specialty roadmap' types section, no 'tips for presenting' section. NN/g: cite, never mirror its components list or its 6 roadmapping steps (goals, inputs, themes, prioritize, visualize, revisit). Our order is evidence -> rewrite -> RICE -> HEART -> horizons -> ownership -> example -> cadence. QA checks 5-gram overlap with the beats page (max 5%).

CONFLICTS for the orchestrator: (1) home.ts embedded team '2–5 designers… shipping features every sprint' vs hub 'ongoing UX consulting as an embedded design team… weekly advisory sessions and quarterly roadmap reviews' + 'UX consulting does not include design work' (follow the hub, no designer count). (2) home.ts pricing shows no UX consulting card (hub $5,000–$15,000 = same as the UX audit card). (3) docs/content-system/fingerprints.json: the entries for usability-testing-cost-per-participant and ecommerce-ux-audit were appended inside the 'fields' array instead of 'posts'; the orchestrator should move them and append this post to 'posts'.
Template CTA check (lesson 2026-10-14): MOFU CTA is case study + consultation; the hub priceRange '$5,000–$15,000' matches this post's offer, so there is no price conflict if the template prints it.
